title: Equations Using Reciprocal Functions
subject: mathematics

theory.introduction: Equations involving secant, cosecant, and cotangent can often be rewritten using their reciprocal relationships.

content.text: Secant is the reciprocal of cosine, cosecant is the reciprocal of sine, and cotangent is the reciprocal of tangent.
These functions are undefined whenever their denominator is zero. Domain restrictions must be respected while solving.

formulas.name: Reciprocal Identities
formulas.explanation: These identities convert reciprocal functions into familiar trigonometric functions.

examples.question: Solve sec(x) = 2 for 0 ≤ x < 2π.
examples.solution: Rewrite as cos(x) = 1/2. Therefore x = π/3 and 5π/3.

key_ideas: Do not include values where the original function is undefined.
misconceptions: Checking only the transformed equation instead of the original one.
